traceability.notes: The story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION defines requirements for validating the syntax and format of @story and @req annotations, including path patterns, REQ-* identifier format, multi-line handling, flexible whitespace, and specific, example-based error messages, and requires integration with existing function/branch rules and thorough tests. The src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts rule implements these behaviors in detail: it normalizes comment lines, accumulates multi-line annotation values, validates @story paths against a strict docs/stories/*.story.md pattern (rejecting traversal), validates @req IDs against a REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+ regex, and uses helper functions to generate precise error messages that echo offending values and expected examples. The rule’s meta section uses ESLint best practices (messageIds, type "problem", fixable: "code"), and it’s wired into the plugin via src/index.ts, with recommended/strict configs applying it alongside the other traceability rules. The dedicated Jest RuleTester suite tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts is explicitly tied to this story and covers both the documented valid and invalid examples, asserting messageIds, message content, and auto-fix output for suffix-normalization cases. Running npm test with Jest completes without reported failures in this environment, so the format validation behavior is tested and passing. Based on this concrete code and test evidence, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied, so the story is fully implemented (PASSED).
